claims.text: Geometric confinement within mesoporous supports limits atomic diffusion during nucleation.
Limited atomic diffusion forces nearly simultaneous nucleation of diverse noble-metal species.
Nearly simultaneous nucleation produces uniform, single-phase high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Pt, Ir, Ru, Rh, and Pd salt precursors can be uniformly impregnated into mesoporous gamma-Al2O3.
The proposed synthesis rapidly heats the impregnated support to approximately 923 K under an inert atmosphere.
Smaller, well-controlled pores provide stronger spatial confinement than larger or less-controlled pores.
Mesopore confinement restricts atomic migration during nanoparticle nucleation.
Spatial confinement causes different metal species to nucleate nearly simultaneously within a limited volume.
Convergent nucleation suppresses phase segregation and enforces homogeneous elemental distribution.
Strong confinement will yield single-phase, compositionally homogeneous nanoparticles.
Strong confinement will preserve high noble-metal surface exposure.
Weaker confinement will produce greater phase segregation and more heterogeneous elemental distributions.
Without effective confinement, extended atomic mobility causes phase segregation and nonuniform nanoparticle morphology.
The proposed mechanism applies when noble-metal precursors can be uniformly impregnated and thermally activated inside mesoporous supports.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when confinement is insufficient or precursor-decomposition kinetics dominate alloy formation.
The quantitative relationship between pore-size distribution and nucleation kinetics is not established.
